questionText:
The following question consists of an incomplete sentence or a sentence that is split into four parts. All four parts are jumbled up and are named P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Arrange the jumbled parts of the sentence and find out which of the four combinations from the given options will correctly complete the sentence.

In the shops of Cambodia, Kulwant Singh______________________particularly financial ones.

P: of our elephant-headed God of success, Ganesha

Q: who was likely to be a counterpart

R: missed the image of any God

S: presiding over all our enterprises
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is “QPSR”

Key Points

  • Clause 'Q' is the first statement because we use 'who' for Kulwant Singh.
  • Clause 'Q' and 'P' is a pair (counterpart - of)
  • Clause 'S' is dependent on clause 'P', Thus, clause 'S' is the third statement.
  • Clause 'R' gives further information for the concluding statement.

Hence, the correct answer is “In the shops of Cambodia, Kulwant Singh, who was likely to be a counterpart of our elephant-headed God of success, Ganesha, presiding over all our enterprises, missed the image of any god, particularly financial ones.”

Additional Information

When we are doing Sentence Rearrangement & Para jumbles, we have to keep three things in our mind:

  1. Identify the introductory and concluding sentences.
  2. After identifying the first and last sentences, the next task is to trace the flow of information the author used. By doing this, you will be able to see the purpose of all the paragraphs, which by default will prompt you to develop a sequence between the sentences.
  3. 'For solving parajumbles, combining statements based on particular characteristics or indicators works well.

questionText:
In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.

Everyone have his own ideas about the best way to bring up children.
solutionExplanation:
The erroneous part is "Everyone have his"

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the usage of "Everyone have his" is incorrect instead of this we need to use "Everyone has his"
  • According to grammar, Whenever we have a singular noun as a subject then, we need to use a singular verb hence, "everyone" is a singular subject so we need to use "has"
  • Let's see an example-
    • Everyone knows who stole it, but they're all afraid to tell anyone.

So the correct sentence is- Everyone has his own ideas about the best way to bring up children.

questionText:
Give a single word that substitutes for the following expression.

Giving undue favours to ones own kith and kin
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is: Nepotism.

Key Points

  • The word "Nepotism" refers to the practice of giving undue favors, jobs, or opportunities to one's own family members or close relatives, often disregarding their qualifications or merit. (परिचितों या रिश्तेदारों को अनुचित लाभ देना)
    • Example: The manager was accused of nepotism after promoting his cousin to a high-ranking position despite her lack of experience.
  • The word "Kinship" refers to the state of being related to someone, especially by blood or family ties. (रिश्तेदारी)
    • Example: The sense of kinship among the members of the community made them support each other during tough times.
  • Although "Kinship" and "Nepotism" are related to family, "Nepotism" specifically refers to favoritism shown due to family ties in professional or political contexts.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Nepotism.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Kinship (रिश्तेदारी): The quality or state of being related by blood or shared characteristics.
    • Example: The kinship between the two families helped them resolve their disputes amicably.
  • Corruption (भ्रष्टाचार): Dishonest or unethical conduct, especially by a person in power, often involving bribery.
    • Example: The government vowed to take strict measures to eliminate corruption from public offices.
  • Favouritism (पक्षपात): Showing undue preference or partiality towards someone over others, often unfairly.
    • Example: The teacher was accused of favouritism for always praising the same group of students.

questionText:

    • Example: She faced a dilemma about whether to move to a new city for a better job or stay close to her family.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Dilemma.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Solution (समाधान): A means of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation.
    • Example: The team worked together to find a solution to the issue.

  • Harmony (सद्भाव): Agreement or concord.

questionText:
Direction: Find out which part has an error and mark it as your answer. If there is no error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

We need to buy a few more pieces of furnitures (A) / for the bedroom say, a new cupboard (B) / and a bedside table. (C) / No error (D)
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is- '(A).'

Key Points

  • The error lies in Part (A) of the sentence.
  • Furniture is an uncountable noun and it does not have a plural form.
  • We commonly use 'piece of furniture' to refer to one or more item or to refer to different kinds of furniture.
    • Example: The pieces of furniture serve a dual purpose as a cupboard and as a table.
  • Therefore, the use of 'furnitures' in Part (A) of the sentence should be replaced by 'furniture' to make it grammatically correct.
  • Hence, the correct answer is '(A).'
    • Correct sentence: We need to buy a few more pieces of furniture for the bedroom say, a new cupboard and a bedside table.

Additional Information

  • Countable nouns, as the term suggests, refer to things that can be counted.
  • They have singular and plural forms.
    • Example: table, tables; month, months; pen, pens.
  • Uncountable nouns cannot be counted.
  • They have a singular form and do not have a plural form.
    • Example: dirt, rice, information, furniture and hair.

Hinglish

  • त्रुटि वाक्य के Part (A) में निहित है।
  • Furniture एक uncountable noun है और इसका plural रूप नहीं है।
  • हम आम तौर पर एक या अधिक वस्तुओं को संदर्भित करने के लिए या विभिन्न प्रकार के फर्नीचर को संदर्भित करने के लिए piece of furniture का उपयोग करते हैं।
    • Example: The pieces of furniture serve a dual purpose as a cupboard and as a table.
  • इसलिए वाक्य के Part (A) में 'furnitures' के प्रयोग को 'furniture' से बदल देना चाहिए ताकि वह व्याकरण की दृष्टि से सही हो।​

questionText:
Direction: In the following question there is a related pair of words given. Each pair is followed by four other pairs of words. Choose the pair from the given option the pair of words that best expresses the relationship like the original pair.

Blurred : Confused
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is 'Muddled : Unclear.'
Key Points

  • Let us see the meanings of the words given in the question- Blurred : Confused:
    • Blurred : difficult to understand or separate clearly. (स्पष्ट रूप से समझना या अलग करना मुश्किल)
    • Confused : difficult to understand. (दुर्बोध, उलझाव-भरा, अस्‍पष्‍ट)
  • In the given pair Blurred : Confused, the synonym of 'Blurred' is 'Confused'.
  • Now, let us explore the meanings of the words from the option:
    • Muddled : badly organized or confusing. (बुरी तरह से संगठित या भ्रमित करने वाला)
    • Unclear : not obvious or easy to see or know. (स्पष्ट या देखने या जानने में आसान नहीं)
    • Dangerous : likely to cause injury or damage. (ख़तरनाक, भयंकर)
    • Culprit : a person who has done something wrong. (अपराधी, दोषी)
    • Cloudy : no clear (गंदा, गँदला)
    • Clarity : the quality of being clear and easy to understand. (स्‍पष्‍टता और सुबोधता)
    • Abatement : the action of abating or being abated; ending or subsiding. (कम करने या कम करने की क्रिया; समाप्त या कम होना)
    • Significant : sufficiently great or important to be worthy of attention; noteworthy. (ध्यान देने योग्य होने के लिए पर्याप्त रूप से महान या महत्वपूर्ण; ध्यान देने योग्य)
  • The synonym of Muddled is Unclear.
  • Complete analogy: Blurred : Confused :: Muddled : Unclear

Additional Information

  • Let us see some more examples of analogies:
    • Pen : Paper
    • Path : Highway
    • Vein : Artery
    • Sculptor : Chisel

questionText:
Direction: The following question, consists of an incomplete sentence or a sentence which is split into four parts. All four parts are jumbled up and are named as P, Q, R and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Arrange the jumbled parts of the sentence and find out which of the four combinations from the given options will correctly complete the sentence.

For some people patriotism ______ as much as to any one country.

P : today man belongs to the whole world

Q : should be condemned because

R : type of patriotism is an evil and it

S : means hatred for other countries, but this
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is 'SRQP.'

Key Points

  • While arranging the parts of the sentence given in options, we have to find some grammatical or contextual connections between them, so let's find out.
  • In this sentence, we can see that there are different parts like Subject, verb, conjunction and continuation of the object.
  • The first part should be S as it is providing the definition of "Patriotism."
  • S should be followed by R as it is saying that "that type of patriotism" is evil.
  • The last part should be P as S is talking about the belonging of a man to the whole world.
  • Thus, forming the basic structure of a sentence.
  • ​​Correct sentence: For some people patriotism means hatred for other countries, but this type of patriotism is an evil and it should be condemned because today man belongs to the whole world as much as to any one country.

Additional Information

  • Before rearranging parts of the sentence, it is very important to read them carefully.
  • It is very important to analyse the use of a determiner and conjunction in such cases.
  • This confusion can be eradicated by practising more and more questions of Sentence Jumbles.

Hinglish

  • विकल्पों में दिए गए वाक्य के भागों को व्यवस्थित करते समय हमें उनके बीच कुछ व्याकरणिक या प्रासंगिक संबंध खोजने होंगे, तो आइए जानें।
  • इस वाक्य में, हम देख सकते हैं कि Subject, verb, conjunction and continuation of the object जैसे विभिन्न भाग हैं।
  • पहला भाग S होना चाहिए क्योंकि यह "Patriotism" की परिभाषा प्रदान कर रहा है।
  • S के बाद R आना चाहिए क्योंकि यह कह रहा है कि"that type of patriotism", evil है।
  • अंतिम भाग P होना चाहिए क्योंकि S एक आदमी के पूरी दुनिया से संबंधित होने की बात कर रहा है।
  • इस प्रकार, एक वाक्य की मूल संरचना का निर्माण हैं।

questionText:
In the following items, each passage consists of six sentences. The first sentence (S1) and the final sentence (S6) are given. The middle four sentences in each have been removed and jumbled up. These are labelled P, Q, R and S. You are required to find out the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

S1: To a foreign learner, English pronunciation presents the greatest difficulty.
P: Words are spell in one way and pronounced in another.
Q: For instance 'u' has different pronunciations in 'but', 'put', 'build' and 'bury'.
​R: The English language is notoriously un-phonetic.
S: The same letters give different sounds in different words.
S6: But a knowledge of Phonetics will help a great deal in learning correct English pronunciation.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is "RPSQ".

Key Points

  • The passage starts with the difficulty of English pronunciation for a foreign learner.
  • Sentence R expands on the reason why it's difficult: English is un-phonetic or doesn't strictly follow pronunciation rules.
  • Sentence P gives a detailed explanation about what is highlighted in sentence R: words being spelled one way and pronounced in a different way.
  • Sentence S further expands the issue, indicating that the same letters can give different sounds in different words.
  • Sentence Q provides examples about what is stated in sentence S - how the letter 'u' can be pronounced differently.
  • S6 concludes that even if English pronunciation is tricky, knowing Phonetics can drastically aid in learning it.

So, the sequence is RPSQ.

Additional Information

The correct sequence for the middle four sentences should be:

R: The English language is notoriously un-phonetic. P: Words are spelled in one way and pronounced in another. S: The same letters give different sounds in different words. Q: For instance 'u' has different pronunciations in 'but', 'put', 'build' and 'bury'.

questionText: Go through the sentence and find out which one's grammatically correct.

options.text: My father helped me to clean the room.
My father helped me cleaning the room.
My father helped me clean the room.
My father helped me cleaned the room.

solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is "My father helped me clean the room."

Key Points

  • When we use the verb "help" followed by an object (in this case, "me"), the infinitive form of the verb that describes the main action can be used with or without "to".
  • In this sentence "helped" is the main verb, "me" is the object (the person receiving the help), and "clean" is the infinitive form of the verb without "to," indicating the action my father assisted me with.

Therefore, the correct answer is "option 3".

questionText:
Select the most appropriate adverb to fill in the blank.

The correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

questionText:
Which word or words explain the meaning of the following idioms:

All agog

The correct answer is option 4) i.e. Full of interest and excitement.

    • Unmoved means not moved; not emotionally affected.
      For example, "Abramovich was as unmoved as ever as he looked on."
    • Praise someone means to glorify someone especially by the attribution of perfections.
      For example, "Praise the Lord."
  • Hence, "Full of interest and excitement" is the meaning of "all agog"
  • The synonyms of 'agog' are agape, anticipant, anticipatory, expectant.
  • We can use "all agog" in a sentence as:
    • "Their family was gathered around them, all agog at their accomplishments."


  • The word 'agog' is derived from the Middle French phrase "en gogues", meaning "in a state of mirth."
  • 'Mirth' means gladness as shown by or accompanied with laughter.
  • The "gog" part of the word might make one wonder if "agog" has a connection to the verb goggle, meaning "to stare with wide or protuberant eyes, as in the manner of one who is intensely excited about something."
  • The first reference to 'agog' in English is in Nicolas Udall's (an English playwright) "The apophthegmes of Erasmus" in 1542.
    • "Beeying set agog to thinke all the worlde otemele."
  • The first sighting of 'all agog' is in William Cowper's "The Diverting History of John Gilpin", 1782:
    • "So three doors off [away] the chaise stayed,
      Where they did all get in;
      Six precious souls, and all agog
      To dash through thick and thin."

questionText:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error mark 'No error' as your answer.

Despite of her fear (A)/, she wrapped her arms (B)/ around him (C)./ No error(D)
solutionExplanation:
Here the correct answer is A.
Key Points:-
  • In the above-given sentence, the error is in part A.
  • It is so because the preposition 'of' is never used with despite.
  • 'In spite of' and 'despite' mean the same, the only difference being that preposition 'of' is not used with despite.
  • Meaning of In spite of and despite - Without being affected by the particular factor mentioned.
  • For Examples:-
    • In spite of being late, he was allowed to enter the office.
    • Despite being late, he was allowed to enter the office.
  • Therefore, 'of' will be removed from the above-given sentence.

Hence, the correct sentence is 'Despite her fear, she wrapped her arms around him'.

  • ऊपर दिए गए वाक्य में त्रुटि भाग A में है ।
  • ऐसा इसलिए है क्योंकि पूर्वसर्ग 'of' का despite के साथ कभी भी प्रयोग नहीं किया जाता है।
  • 'In spite of' और 'despite' का अर्थ एक ही है, केवल अंतर यह है कि 'of' पूर्वसर्ग का प्रयोग despite के साथ नहीं किया जाता है।
  • In spite of और despite का अर्थ - उल्लेखित विशेष कारक से प्रभावित हुए बिना ।
  • उदाहरण के लिए:-
    • In spite of being late, he was allowed to enter the office.
    • Despite being late, he was allowed to enter the office.
  • अतः ऊपर दिए गए वाक्य में से 'of' हटा दिया जाएगा।
    ​

इसलिए, सही वाक्य है 'Despite her fear, she wrapped her arms around him'.

questionText:
Select the most appropriate word from the options against each number:- Those living in the slums are(1)_______ and tough because they are totally (2)______ to the vagaries and hardships of life. The rising sun (3)_______ the day and the setting sun closes the day for them. It is like a drama where the curtain(4)______ up in the morning and comes down in the evening. They don't (5)_______ hypertension and heart attacks because there is, after all (6)_______ to worry about.

What would come in place of (2)?
solutionExplanation:
Explanation

The correct option is 3 i.e. exposed.

'Exposed' is an adjective. It refers to being in a vulnerable position or situation.

  • The passage mainly speaks of hardships of the slum dwellers. Phrases like 'vagaries and hardships, 'drama,' 'tough,' etc. refer to the state of living for these people. Exposed clearly refers to their vulnerability to the various problems that they may face.

​

Lets look at what the other words would mean:

  • Independent means free from outside control, which is not the case for these people.
  • Dependent means requiring someone or something for financial or other support. This could be a plausible option, however, the use of this in the context would be incorrect.
  • This is because, they are 'not dependent on hardships'. They are just dependent in general, for financial support.
  • Tried means to make an attempt or effort to do something. Here again, the slum dwellers are no 'trying to have hardships' and therefore, it would not be a correct fit for the sentence.
    ​

Therefore, the correct statement would read: "...they are totally (2) exposed to the vagaries and hardships of life."

They don't (5)_______ hypertension and heart attacks because there is, after all (6)_______ to worry about.

What would come in place of (3)?
solutionExplanation:
Explanation

The correct option is 4 i.e. brings.

'Brings is a verb. It refers to causing (something). Also, 'brings' is indicative and indicates the coming of the day for the people and that fact is important.

  • The passage mainly speaks of hardships of the slum dwellers. Phrases like 'vagaries and hardships, 'drama,' 'tough,' etc. refer to the state of living for these people.
  • The word 'brings' in this case, would mean that the 'rising sun' brings the 'day'; it causes the day to begin and bring with it it's elements.
  • The sentence also ends with speaking of the 'setting sun' as 'closing' the day.

​

Lets look at what the other words would mean:

  • Ends means the termination of a state or situation. In this case, the rising sun would not mean the end of the day.
  • Herald means a sign that (something) is about to happen.
  • This is a plausible alternative. However, the second half of the sentence - 'closing' would indicate the 'beginning' as well. In this case, 'brings' would be a better word to use.
  • Continued means ongoing action. Here again, the rising sun is the beginning of an action or day, and could not possibly mean continuation of the day. It would make less sense in the sentence.
    ​

Therefore, the correct statement would read: "The rising sun (3) brings the day and the setting sun closes the day for them."

​

questionText:

Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal on Wednesday said India is on the path of ______(1)______ and things are falling back into place, and asked industry to focus on quality and productivity as they ______(2)______ both manufacturing and services. “We are on the path of recovery and things are falling back into place…The ______(3)______ and determination that our Indian industry has shown over the last nine months of Covid-19 is truly very encouraging and has shown the world capacity of India and Indian industry,” he said at a webinar on Udyog Manthan organised by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade.

solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is Recovery.

    • Precaution is used when talking about a measure taken in advance to prevent something dangerous, unpleasant, or inconvenient from happening.
    • Cure is used when talking about a substance or treatment that cures a disease or condition.
